usage: 보호하다 (protect) is the standard verb in eco contexts.
Very common compound; pairs with pollution, climate, etc.
환경 also means the conditions around you, not just nature.
to be good for the environment
Use 에 to mark what the effect is on.
examples: 요즘 환경 문제에 관심을 가지는 사람이 많아졌어요.
These days more people have become interested in environmental issues.
관심을 가지다 = to take an interest in.
일회용품을 줄이는 것이 환경을 보호하는 첫걸음이에요.
Reducing disposables is the first step to protecting the environment.
첫걸음 = first step; common in essays.
이 회사는 근무 환경이 좋아서 직원들이 오래 다녀요.
This company has a good work environment, so employees stay long.
환경 used for workplace conditions, not nature.
nuance: 환경 covers both the natural environment (nature, pollution, climate) and the conditions surrounding a person, such as a 근무 환경 (work environment) or 가정 환경 (home environment). In intermediate texts it most often appears in discussions of ecology and society. Pair it with 보호하다 for protection and 오염되다 for pollution.
mistakes: Using 환경 only for nature — it also means general surroundings/conditions (근무 환경, 주변 환경).
Saying 환경을 좋다 — use 환경이 좋다 (the environment is good) or 환경에 좋다 (good for the environment).

usage: 쌓다 (to pile up) is the natural verb, not 만들다.
전문 = specialty; common in job descriptions.
풍부하다 = abundant; a compliment about someone.
Useful when talking about understanding a topic.
examples: 책을 많이 읽으면 다양한 지식을 쌓을 수 있어요.
If you read a lot of books, you can build up varied knowledge.
쌓다 collocates naturally with 지식.
이 일을 하려면 어느 정도의 전문 지식이 필요해요.
To do this job you need a certain level of specialized knowledge.
어느 정도 = a certain degree.
배경 지식이 있으면 기사를 이해하기가 훨씬 쉬워요.
If you have background knowledge, articles are much easier to understand.
이해하기가 쉽다 = easy to understand.
nuance: 지식 is knowledge as accumulated information and facts, the kind you gain from study or experience. It differs from 지혜 (wisdom), which is the good judgment to use that knowledge well. The everyday verb is 지식을 쌓다, picturing knowledge as something you stack up over time.
mistakes: Saying 지식을 만들다 — knowledge is accumulated (쌓다), not 'made'.
Confusing 지식 (knowledge/facts) with 지혜 (wisdom/judgment).

usage: 받다 (receive) is the standard verb from the learner's side.
With 하다 it becomes a verb meaning to teach/train.
공 = public; contrasts with 사교육 (private education).
examples: 한국 부모들은 자녀 교육에 정말 많은 관심을 가져요.
Korean parents take a great deal of interest in their children's education.
자녀 = one's children (formal).
회사에서 신입 사원들을 대상으로 교육을 진행했어요.
The company carried out training for the new employees.
교육 also means workplace training, not just school.
좋은 교육을 받는 것은 모든 아이의 권리예요.
Receiving a good education is every child's right.
권리 = right; common in social topics.
nuance: 교육 means education in a broad sense, covering schooling, parenting, and on-the-job training. From the learner's side you say 교육을 받다 (receive education); from the teacher's side 교육하다 or 교육을 시키다. In Korea the contrast between 공교육 (public) and 사교육 (private tutoring) is a frequent social topic.
mistakes: Saying 교육을 하다 when you mean to study — that means to provide training; learners use 교육을 받다.
Limiting 교육 to schools — it also covers corporate 교육 (training sessions).

usage: to believe in / practice a religion
Common way to ask 종교가 있어요? = Do you have a religion?
자유 = freedom; appears in civic/social texts.
Refers to attending services, volunteering, etc.
examples: 혹시 믿는 종교가 있으세요?
Do you happen to follow any religion?
Polite way to ask about someone's faith.
한국에는 다양한 종교가 평화롭게 공존하고 있어요.
In Korea various religions coexist peacefully.
공존하다 = to coexist.
저는 특별히 믿는 종교는 없지만 다른 종교를 존중해요.
I don't follow any particular religion, but I respect others'.
존중하다 = to respect.
nuance: 종교 is the general term for religion as a system of belief, while a 종교인 is a religious person. Asking 종교가 있어요? is a normal, neutral question, though faith is treated as fairly private. The verb pair 종교를 믿다 literally means 'to believe a religion,' covering both holding the faith and practicing it.
mistakes: Saying 종교를 하다 — you 믿다 (believe/practice) a religion, you don't 'do' it.
Confusing 종교 (religion in general) with 교회 (a church building/Protestant church).

usage: -가 turns 예술 into the person; covers all art forms.
전통 = tradition; e.g. dance, music, crafts.
Add -적 to make the adjective-like form (예술적인 감각).
examples: 이 미술관에서는 다양한 예술 작품을 감상할 수 있어요.
At this gallery you can appreciate various works of art.
감상하다 = to appreciate/enjoy (art).
그 사람은 예술적 감각이 정말 뛰어나요.
That person has truly outstanding artistic sense.
예술적 감각 = artistic sense.
요리도 하나의 예술이라고 생각해요.
I think cooking is also a form of art.
하나의 = one (kind of); common framing.
nuance: 예술 refers to the arts as a whole, including 미술 (visual art), 음악 (music), 무용 (dance), and 문학 (literature). It is broader than 미술, which means painting and visual art specifically. For the adjective sense, use 예술적 (artistic), as in 예술적인 표현 (artistic expression).
mistakes: Using 예술 only for paintings — that narrower meaning is 미술; 예술 covers all art forms.
Saying 예술스럽다 — the natural adjective form is 예술적이다 / 예술적인.

usage: 작품 = work; the standard pairing for novels, poems.
Put the culture/era before 문학 to specify.
고전 = classic; contrasts with 현대 문학 (modern).
examples: 대학에서 한국 문학을 전공하고 싶어요.
I want to major in Korean literature at university.
전공하다 = to major in.
이 소설은 한국 현대 문학의 대표 작품이에요.
This novel is a representative work of modern Korean literature.
대표 작품 = representative work.
문학을 통해 그 시대 사람들의 삶을 엿볼 수 있어요.
Through literature you can glimpse the lives of people of that era.
-을 통해 = through; 엿보다 = to glimpse.
nuance: 문학 means literature as an art form built from language: novels, poetry, drama, and essays. It is one branch under 예술 and is the academic word, not casual; for everyday reading people just say 소설 (novel) or 책 (book). Note that 문학 (literature) sounds similar to 문화 (culture) but the two are distinct.
mistakes: Mixing up 문학 (literature) with 문화 (culture) — they differ by one syllable but mean different things.
Using 문학 for a single novel — a specific book is 소설/작품; 문학 is the whole field.

usage: 외국 (foreign) + 어; 어 is the shorter combining form.
모국 = homeland; the language you grew up with.
examples: 새로운 언어를 배우는 것은 쉽지 않지만 정말 재미있어요.
Learning a new language isn't easy, but it's really fun.
Contrast set up with -지만 (but).
언어는 그 나라의 문화를 이해하는 열쇠예요.
Language is the key to understanding a country's culture.
열쇠 = key (metaphorical).
그분은 언어 능력이 뛰어나서 통역사로 일해요.
She has excellent language ability, so she works as an interpreter.
통역사 = interpreter.
nuance: 언어 is the abstract concept of language in general, while a specific language usually takes the suffix 어 (한국어 Korean, 영어 English, 일본어 Japanese). So you study 한국어 but discuss 언어 as a phenomenon. The native-Korean near-synonym 말 is more casual and also means 'speech/words.'
mistakes: Saying 한국언어 — a named language uses the suffix 어: 한국어, not 한국언어.
Using 언어 for casual 'words/talk' — that everyday sense is 말.

usage: Describe size with 많다/적다, not 크다.
감소 = decrease; a major social topic.
고령 = old age; e.g. 고령 인구 증가.
examples: 서울은 인구가 많아서 항상 복잡해요.
Seoul has a large population, so it's always crowded.
Use 많다 for population size.
요즘 한국은 인구 감소 문제가 심각해요.
These days population decline is a serious problem in Korea.
심각하다 = serious.
이 지역은 젊은 인구가 점점 줄고 있어요.
The young population in this area is gradually shrinking.
점점 = gradually; 줄다 = decrease.
nuance: 인구 means the number of people living in a place, the population. Describe its size with 많다 (many) or 적다 (few), and its change with 늘다 (increase) or 줄다 (decrease); avoid 크다/작다, which suit physical size. In contemporary Korea, 인구 감소 and 고령화 (aging) are constant news themes.
mistakes: Saying 인구가 크다 — population is 많다/적다 (many/few), not 'big/small'.
Confusing 인구 (population) with 인기 (popularity) — they look similar but are unrelated.

usage: 주민 = residents; pairs naturally with 지역.
사회 = society; 지역 사회 = the local community.
examples: 이 지역은 교통이 편리해서 살기 좋아요.
This area has convenient transit, so it's good to live in.
살기 좋다 = good to live in.
지역마다 사투리와 음식이 조금씩 달라요.
Dialects and food differ a little from region to region.
지역마다 = every region; 사투리 = dialect.
지역 주민들이 환경 보호 활동에 적극적으로 참여했어요.
Local residents actively took part in environmental protection activities.
적극적으로 = actively.
nuance: 지역 means a geographic region or local area, and by extension the local community (지역 사회). It is more formal and neutral than 동네, which is your immediate, familiar neighborhood. Use 지역 for administrative or news-style talk (지역 경제, 지역 주민) and 동네 for the friendly block where you live.
mistakes: Confusing 지역 (any region/area) with 지방 — 지방 specifically means the provinces outside the capital.
Using 지역 for your cozy neighborhood — that warmer sense is 동네.

usage: With 하다 it becomes the verb (전화를 발명하다).
품 = item; the thing that was invented.
examples: 전화는 인류 역사에서 아주 중요한 발명이에요.
The telephone is a very important invention in human history.
인류 = humankind.
에디슨은 전구를 발명한 것으로 유명해요.
Edison is famous for inventing the light bulb.
-(으)ㄴ 것으로 유명하다 = famous for.
그 학생은 재미있는 발명품을 만들어서 상을 받았어요.
That student made an interesting invention and won a prize.
발명품 = the invented item; 상을 받다 = win a prize.
nuance: 발명 means inventing something that did not exist before, like a machine or device, and 발명품 is the resulting product. It contrasts with 발견 (discovery), which is finding something that already existed. So you 발명하다 a telephone but 발견하다 a new planet or law of nature.
mistakes: Confusing 발명 (invention — creating something new) with 발견 (discovery — finding what existed).
Saying 발명을 하다 for a physical item — the made object is 발명품; 발명하다 is the act.

usage: With 하다 it means to come across/realize.
새로운 = new; common in science talk.
Passive form when the discoverer is unstated.
examples: 과학자들이 새로운 행성을 발견했어요.
Scientists discovered a new planet.
행성 = planet.
그 그림은 한 농부에 의해 우연히 발견되었어요.
That painting was discovered by chance by a farmer.
-에 의해 = by (agent); 발견되다 passive.
여행하면서 나 자신에 대한 새로운 점을 발견했어요.
While traveling I discovered something new about myself.
발견 also covers realizing things, not just objects.
nuance: 발견 means discovering or finding something that already existed but was unknown, whether a planet, an old document, or a fact about yourself. Contrast it with 발명 (invention), which creates something brand new. The verb 발견하다 also extends to figuratively 'realizing' something, as in noticing a new side of a person.
mistakes: Confusing 발견 (discovery — finding what existed) with 발명 (invention — creating new).
Forgetting the passive 발견되다 — use it when you don't name who discovered it.

usage: 발달하다 is the natural verb for tech progress.
Fixed pairing in news and policy talk.
기술 also means a practical hands-on skill.
examples: 요즘은 기술이 빠르게 발달해서 생활이 편리해졌어요.
These days technology develops fast, so life has become convenient.
발달하다 = to develop/advance.
그는 요리 기술이 뛰어나서 유명한 식당에서 일해요.
He has outstanding cooking skills, so he works at a famous restaurant.
기술 here = practical skill, not high-tech.
새로운 기술 덕분에 많은 일이 자동화되고 있어요.
Thanks to new technology, many tasks are being automated.
-덕분에 = thanks to; 자동화 = automation.
nuance: 기술 spans two senses: large-scale technology (과학 기술, IT 기술) and an individual's practical skill or technique (요리 기술, 운전 기술). Context tells them apart. For technology advancing, the idiomatic verb is 발달하다, and for a person acquiring a skill it is 기술을 배우다 or 기술을 익히다.
mistakes: Using 기술 only for high-tech — it equally means a hands-on personal skill (요리 기술).
Saying 기술이 발전되다 for a person's skill — for tech progress use 발달하다.

usage: With 하다, the verb for in-depth academic study.
원 = staff member; person who does research.
examples: 그 교수님은 평생 암 치료를 연구했어요.
That professor researched cancer treatment all his life.
평생 = one's whole life.
이번 연구 결과는 학계에서 큰 주목을 받았어요.
These research findings drew great attention in academia.
학계 = academic world; 주목을 받다 = draw attention.
대학원에서 한국어 교육에 대해 연구하고 있어요.
I'm researching Korean language education in graduate school.
-에 대해 = about; 대학원 = grad school.
nuance: 연구 means systematic academic or scientific research, deeper and more formal than everyday 공부 (studying). You 공부 a textbook to learn it, but you 연구 a question to produce new knowledge. It pairs with institutions and outcomes: 연구실 (lab), 연구원 (researcher), 연구 결과 (findings).
mistakes: Using 연구 for ordinary studying — daily school study is 공부; 연구 is investigative research.
Saying 연구를 하다 then 'making' results — findings are 연구 결과가 나오다 (results come out).
